{% raw %}
`ps`: list the processes.

## Synopsis

<strong>ps</strong>

## Description

<strong>ps</strong> lists every process, one a line, under a header:

<strong>PID</strong>
: The process's id.

<strong>PPID</strong>
: Its parent's id.

<strong>PGID</strong>
: Its process group.

<strong>STATE</strong>
: <strong>running</strong> (it can run), <strong>sleeping</strong> (blocked in a system call: waiting for input, a child or a timer), or <strong>zombie</strong> (it has ended and its parent has not waited for it).

<strong>COMMAND</strong>
: The program's path, then its arguments.

## Notes

There are no options; arguments are ignored. There are no users, times or memory figures to show.

## See also

<strong>kill</strong>(1), <strong>free</strong>(1), <strong>uptime</strong>(1)
